name: White and blue 'CARGO' (777F)
description: Fuselage: White, with a royal-blue upper aft fuselage from over the wing root back to the tail cone, its lower edge sweeping down below the middle of the side behind the wing and up again toward the tail. Titles: 'CARGO' in thin, widely spaced dark-gray capitals low on the forward fuselage ahead of the wing; 'operated by Polar Air Cargo' in small print by the nose. Tail: plain white fin. Engines: white.

history: On Polar's two 777-F16s, N702GT and N703GT, built for LAN Cargo. Already in this scheme in 2020 and 2021 (Commons), before AirHistory.net's captions put them with Polar (July 2022), so it isn't Polar's own design: an anonymous 'CARGO' scheme with the operator in small print. Aeroxplorer labels 2023–2024 photos of N702GT 'Southern Air Cargo' (Southern Air is Atlas Air's other subsidiary); no source says the scheme was Southern Air's.
notes: Drawn on the widebody shape from N702GT (right, 2023; left, 2021) and N703GT (2020, 2023). The small operator line is too small to read in the photos; its wording follows earlier notes ('operated by Polar Air Cargo') and is low confidence. Re-checked 2026-11-15 against N702GT (2023-01-17) and N703GT (2023-03-08): the blue field's forward and lower edges are one sweeping curve (smooth, its aft corner kept); titles' places and lengths agree.
